feed.summary: Sempra Infrastructure has secured a 20-year agreement to supply Petrobras with approximately 0.8 million tonnes per annum of liquefied natural gas (LNG). feed.title: NIVA Calls for Ticketmaster Breakup, 50% Cap on Live Nation Tour Control
feed.summary: The National Independent Venue Association (NIVA) has urged a federal court to reject the Justice Department's proposed Live Nation settlement. NIVA's recommendations include breaking up Live Nation and Ticketmaster, preventing Live Nation from promoting more than 50% of any major artist's U.S. tour, and divesting Live Nation's artist management businesses. The association argues that the current settlement's restrictions are too narrow and fail to address Live Nation's extensive market power, particularly its influence over tour control and ticket pricing.

feed.title: GLP-1 Pioneer Prof. Jens Juul Holst Joins Tema ETFs As A Scientific Advisor
feed.summary: Tema ETFs has appointed Prof. Jens Juul Holst, a pioneer in GLP-1 research, to its Scientific Advisory Board. Prof. Holst's discoveries of the GLP-1 hormone have been crucial in developing treatments for obesity and type 2 diabetes, including drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy. His expertise will support Tema's focus on breakthrough life sciences investing, particularly through their Heart & Health ETF (HRTS), which targets companies fighting obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases.

feed.title: Dominion, NextEra double merger bill credits for residential customers
feed.summary: Dominion and NextEra have improved their merger offer to the Virginia State Corporation Commission, proposing to double monthly bill credits for residential customers from two to four years, primarily by reallocating credits from data centers. The revised deal also includes building a new NextEra headquarters in Richmond, creating 600 jobs, extending job protections for Dominion employees for five years, and committing $100 million to energy-focused job training programs and increased funding for EnergyShare. Critics like Clean Virginia remain concerned that the merger's corporate structure could expose Virginia ratepayers to significant risks, particularly given NextEra's involvement in competitive markets.

feed.title: SmartPM Expands Integration with Autodesk Forma® Build’s RFI and Submittal Data
feed.summary: SmartPM Technologies has expanded its integration with Autodesk Forma® Build, allowing construction teams to integrate RFI and submittal data directly into SmartPM’s schedule analytics engine. This enhancement provides greater context around schedule performance and project risk by connecting critical project information traditionally evaluated across separate workflows. The integration aims to transform fragmented construction data into actionable project intelligence, helping teams prioritize and address potential delays.

feed.title: Citigroup Sees ROTCE Beating Guidance as Markets, Cards and Services Gain

feed.title: Why SLB Stock Slumped Today
feed.summary: SLB stock fell by nearly 5% due to the closure of a major Saudi Arabian oil pipeline following drone attacks, a development that rattled investors. Citigroup issued an analyst note highlighting SLB's high exposure to the Saudi market and the potential negative impact on drilling activity if the shutdown is prolonged. This event is seen as an escalation of the Iran conflict, adding to volatility in the energy sector.

feed.title: CenterPoint Energy discloses customer data breach in SEC filing
feed.summary: CenterPoint Energy has disclosed in an SEC filing that it experienced a customer data breach in September, following an online post claiming to have obtained customer information. The utility company has activated its cybersecurity protocols and engaged third-party experts, determining that an unauthorized party accessed personal information through one of its external systems. While electric and gas services remain operational and the company does not anticipate a material financial impact, it expects to incur expenses that cybersecurity insurance is believed to offset.

feed.title: Lockheed Martin wins three defense contracts worth over $1.3bn

feed.title: Northrop Grumman gets $34 million Navy contract modification
feed.summary: Northrop Grumman Systems Corp. has received a $34.3 million contract modification from the U.S. Department of War, increasing the ceiling of an existing contract for military helicopter components. This modification will expand the procurement of UH-1Y and AH-1Z Helicopter Link-16 A-Kits, B-Kits, and associated spare parts. Work on the contract is expected to be completed by March 2027 and will be distributed across multiple locations in the U.S.

feed.title: Big Tech Issued About $220 Billion of Bonds. Alphabet and Meta Show How AI Is Warping the Credit Market
feed.summary: Big Tech companies like Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle have issued approximately $220 billion in bonds over the past year to fund data center expansion for AI. This massive bond issuance is starting to distort the credit market, even for high-quality borrowers, as investors demand more compensation for duration and supply. While this isn't a solvency warning for companies like Alphabet and Meta, it serves as a price signal, making financing more expensive and raising the bar for returns on AI investments.

feed.title: Citigroup CFO Luchetti expects equity return above 11% this year
feed.summary: Citigroup's CFO, Gonzalo Luchetti, announced that the bank anticipates its return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) to exceed 11% this year. The bank also plans to increase stock buybacks beyond the $13 billion from 2025 and accelerate about $500 million in investments, including severance for headcount reduction and growth initiatives like marketing for credit cards and wealth management. Luchetti also expects the removal of Mexico's Banamex from Citi's balance sheet next year, resulting in a $9 billion currency translation adjustment loss, while emphasizing a focus on organic growth with potential for small, additive acquisitions.

feed.title: Wells Fargo commercial banking head Manning to retire, Biodrowski to succeed By Reuters
feed.summary: John Manning, Wells Fargo's executive vice president and head of commercial banking market coverage, will retire at the end of the year after over 30 years with the bank. Rob Biodrowski, currently a division executive for the U.S. Midwest, will succeed Manning starting in November. Biodrowski brings more than 20 years of experience in financial services and will lead over 2,000 bankers serving companies with annual revenues from $25 million to $2 billion across the U.S. and Canada.

feed.title: Ford accused of hiding a keyless entry theft risk in new class action lawsuit
feed.summary: A new class action lawsuit has been filed against Ford Motor Co., alleging that the company knowingly sold vehicles equipped with a "Smart Key" passive keyless entry system that is easily defeated by thieves. The lawsuit claims Ford has been aware of this vulnerability since 2011 but failed to disclose it to buyers, leading to increased theft risks and decreased resale values for affected models like the F-150, Bronco, Explorer, Mustang, and Escape. The plaintiff seeks triple damages, a disgorgement of profits, attorney's fees, and an order for Ford to inform current owners about the security flaw.

feed.title: Costco just might have a future in Asheville
feed.summary: Costco has resubmitted plans to build a 166,000-square-foot facility in Asheville's Enka Commerce Park, including a 32-pump gas station and 914 parking spaces. This comes after the retailer withdrew its initial application earlier in the year due to complications with scope, timeline, and costs. The new proposal addresses previous concerns regarding road changes, stormwater infrastructure on a former industrial site, and traffic impact, and will now go before the city's Planning & Zoning Commission and City Council for approval.
